Keywords: Havel and Spree River Stone Castles
RagShortTexts: Ascanian settlement requires land clearance, labour, tools and support before harvest.
Exemptions vary by charter; no single five-year privilege covers all new settlers.

Variants.Content: Bearing the soaring Red Eagle on argent, the House of Ascania established the Margraviate of Brandenburg. Descended from Albert the Bear, co-rulers John I and Otto III drove eastern colonization, called Ostsiedlung, through marshes along the Spree and Havel. Settlers cleared forest and drained bogs, and the towns of Berlin and Cölln grew from those settlements. The Ascanian margraves organized the new land around fortified river crossings and market charters, which gave the region a stable base for trade. Their rivalry with Bohemian kings over the frontier shaped Brandenburg's politics for decades.

Holding the hereditary imperial office of Arch-Chamberlain, the Ascanian margraves commanded electoral status. Their claims pushed the empire's northeastern border toward the Oder River, and each new castle or market charter strengthened their hand against Polish and Bohemian rivals on the eastern frontier.

Settlers clearing woodland in the Brandenburg marches need tools, draught animals and enough food to survive before new fields yield. A charter may offer temporary relief from specified dues, but its terms differ from one settlement to another. A family must hear the actual grant read aloud; no universal five-year exemption feeds everyone who arrives with an axe.
